sourceLine: your founders' simulation work and the questions robotics teams ask before they trust a faster simulator

cards.title: Why Simulation Speed Matters on the Robot Itself
cards.angle: Nvidia's Newton 1.0 (March 2026) sells thousands of parallel environments on datacenter GPUs. Running a simulator on the hardware a robot carries is a different engineering problem, and the two are complements, not rivals.
cards.evidence: The BBC's September 2026 feature reports your simulator running on compute carried by Freddo, with Storey describing it looking about a second ahead across 20,000 combinations, his description rather than a published benchmark. What has to fit the onboard budget and what still belongs in large-scale training is the article.

cards.title: What Legacy Contact Solvers Cost on GPUs
cards.angle: Isaac Sim 6.0 now ships two physics backends, which makes solver architecture a live question in the field. Storey's public position is that many familiar physics algorithms were built before GPUs became central to robot learning.
cards.evidence: Your founders spent a decade each on PhysX and Isaac Sim at Nvidia, and your 2024 round cited an up-to-100x RL training speedup that has no public baseline. A piece showing one contact-heavy task, where the mismatch costs time and what you do differently, would be your first published content and would make the 100x claim checkable.

cards.title: Speed Versus Realism in Sim-to-Real
cards.angle: NEURA partnered with Dassault in April 2026 specifically on the sim-to-real gap, and a faster simulator only helps when the behaviour it teaches survives contact with the real world. Where a simulator accepts approximation is a design decision, not a detail.
cards.evidence: Lu describes Vsim's approach as reduced approximation, and the BBC piece quotes Cambridge's Rika Antonova on the limits of simulated worlds. Freddo's bottle grasp is a demonstration, not proof of transfer across robots; the article is where you accept approximation, where you refuse it, and how you test the difference on hardware.
